headline: SpaceX throttles Ukraine’s military Starlink mid-mission; Berlin’s cabinet clears a watered-down Zuckersteuer; Hamburg opens the first Nord Stream sabotage trial; and French fridge hacks widen to Copeland/Dixell.

stories.title: SpaceX limits Ukraine’s military Starlink above ~160 km/h — missions aborted overnight
facts: Presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov says SpaceX overnight capped StarShield (military Starlink) terminals in motion at 100 mph / 160 km/h, with no prior warning.
Ukraine’s 7th Rapid Response Corps reported link drops of 10–20 seconds already at 110–120 km/h, forcing some drone missions to be cancelled.
Static/ordinary Starlink terminals are said to keep working; the hit is to terminals moving with fast drones used for mid-range strikes.
The timing lands as Trump presses Kyiv to stop strikes on Russian oil infrastructure; Beskrestnov calls a coincidence “obviously” unlikely. SpaceX has not confirmed the change.
stories.whyItMatters: Starlink underpins Ukrainian battlefield comms and drone guidance. A silent speed gate is a soft kill-switch on the most mobile part of that stack, and it lands in the middle of a US–Ukraine political squeeze.

stories.title: Cabinet clears a watered-down Zuckersteuer for sugary drinks from July 2027
facts: The federal cabinet today approved Klingbeil’s Formulierungshilfe for a sugar tax on sweetened drinks — after the Chancellery had blocked a steeper draft earlier this month.
Two tiers only (the third was cut): 26¢/L from 5 g sugar per 100 ml, 32¢/L from 8 g. Pure fruit juice is out; light products stay untaxed.
Independent producers up to 70,000 L/year get special rules; up to 1 million L/year would be fully exempt if the EU clears the state aid.
Full-year take for 2027 is now pegged at about €820m (was €925m); mid-year start means ~€690m in 2027 cash. Bundestag still has to pass it.
stories.whyItMatters: After weeks of coalition friction, Merz’s cabinet locked a thinner health levy that still needs the Bundestag — and an EU nod for the SME carve-out.

stories.title: Nord Stream sabotage trial opens in Hamburg — first criminal case worldwide
facts: Hamburg’s Hanseatic Higher Regional Court opened the first criminal trial over the Sept 2022 Nord Stream blasts this morning; the defendant said nothing in court.
Serhii K. (Serhii/Serhiy Kuznietsov), a former Ukrainian special-forces officer, is accused of leading a seven-person team that planted timed military explosives from the yacht Andromeda.
Charges include a war crime (attack on civilian objects), causing an explosion, destroying structures and disrupting public utilities. He was arrested in Italy in Aug 2025 and extradited in Nov 2025.
Federal prosecutors believe Ukrainian state actors ordered the sabotage; Kyiv denies it. Hearings are listed into Jan 2027, with the case expected to run well beyond that.
stories.whyItMatters: Germany is the first country to put someone in the dock for Europe’s biggest peacetime energy sabotage — while remaining Ukraine’s biggest European backer.

image.alt: Former Ukrainian military officer to stand trial in Germany over Nord Stream sabotage

stories.title: French supermarket fridge hacks widen beyond Danfoss to Copeland/Dixell
facts: After Monday’s Danfoss-linked wave, CERT-FR and French reporting now also name Copeland XWEB and Dixell XWEB remote refrigeration controllers among compromised systems.
An E.Leclerc store near Albi using Dixell gear lost control of its cold rooms early Tuesday; staff found cooling PCs unresponsive around 04:00.
A Copeland spokesperson said a flaw was found in a discontinued, end-of-life controller generation and that the company is working with affected customers.

SOCRadar’s 13 Oct scan still finds ~2,900 internet-exposed Danfoss units in France alone (~65% of ~4,500 worldwide). Claroty had already published deep attack-surface research on both Danfoss and Copeland XWEB in August.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a material update to this week’s cold-chain story: the blast radius is multi-vendor, and internet-facing fridge controllers are now a food-safety issue, not just an OT footnote.

facts.text: Anthropic opens a Singapore office (its fifth in APAC) and signs an MOU with Singapore’s digital ministry on AI safety, evaluation and public-sector adoption — Claude already used at GovTech, Grab and DBS.
Swiss marketplace Ricardo: ~890k customers’ names, postal addresses and phone numbers stolen after odd activity on 7 Oct; emails/passwords not taken. WhatsApp phishing already follows.
AnitaB.org cancels this year’s Grace Hopper Celebration in Anaheim: registrations and sponsorships fell short of covering costs. Fee guidance to registrants by 26 Oct.
Chrome 155 stable (155.0.8059.79/.80) ships 37 security fixes, seven of them Critical — including an ANGLE buffer overflow and UAFs in Browser, PDF, Network, Core, SVG and Media.
CISA put Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2026-104935 on KEV (13 Oct): unauth auth-bypass → remote command exec, used for credential theft. Patch now; Integrity Checker may miss in-memory activity.
Android Auto 18.0 has started rolling out, still gearing up for the larger redesign (9to5Google).
Eintracht Braunschweig: masked intruders (police: likely Hannover 96 ultras) stormed a hall building the derby choreo, stole materials; nobody hurt. Derby 25 Oct; robbery probes opened.
Warriors lock Brandin Podziemski on a 5-year, $110m rookie-scale extension (starts next season ~$18.9m, rises to $25m, mutual option 2031-32).
